Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 26-year-old woman with 3-day history of worsening, predominantly right-periorbital dull/occasionally sharp headache, severity 8/10, associated photophobia, visual “shooting lights,” nausea without vomiting, no fever, neck stiffness, focal deficits, or trauma.  
• Family history strongly positive for migraine.  
• Ibuprofen 3 tablets/day ineffective (sub-therapeutic dose).  

Consistent differential considerations  
– Migraine (likely with aura): high likelihood given location, photophobia, visual phenomena, nausea, female sex, family history.  
– Tension-type headache: moderate likelihood; diffuse pain and work stress but photophobia less typical.  
– Acute sinusitis: low–moderate likelihood; right-eye pain but lacks nasal symptoms.  

Plan agreed in consult  
• Educate patient that presentation most consistent with migraine; could be single episode or evolving pattern.  
• Optimize NSAID dosing: ibuprofen up to 400 mg (two tablets) three times daily OR prescribe naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Option to add paracetamol and/or codeine for additional analgesia (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Initiate headache diary to identify triggers.  
• Safety-net advice: return or call sooner if deterioration, new visual changes, weakness, or systemic symptoms.  
• Routine follow-up in 1–2 weeks; consider prophylactic therapy if headaches become frequent.
